_about: Cook with Nani proof of concept (24 Sept 2026). Every Kutchi string here is a DRAFT. Words marked source 'zafar-24sep' were confirmed by Zafar as right for now (khun, not khand). Sentences only recombine frames already in the content master (Muke {x} khape / Ne {x} / Salamun alaykum / Wa alaikum salaam / Aabhar aanjo / Achija / Arre re / Hedo / Ghan). Cooking verbs have NO Kutchi yet: they are shown as gestures, and listed in docs/cook-with-nani-words.md for the family. Phase A (24 Sept 2026): words with kutchi null are ENGLISH PLACEHOLDERS shown in grey italic until the family supplies the Kutchi (see docs/Nani jo Ghar — Questions for Mum (Round 2 — Cooking).md). 25 Sept 2026: seven more words (ph-no, ph-slowly, ph-quickly, ph-half, ph-full, ph-big, ph-small) came from Zafar written phonetically over chat, temporary and unconfirmed (Mum to confirm). Each has `kutchi` (a readable romanised spelling, shown on screen) and `say` (Zafar's own phonetic spelling, used for the voice only, never shown). 26 Sept 2026: Mum's A8 and Section B answers (docs/kutchi-grammar-notes.md §23-§28) replaced most English placeholders and Zafar's phonetic drafts; every change is listed in docs/cook-word-changes-B.md.

grammar._about: How this language builds sentences. The code only names roles (an order's first line, a list, a counted noun); the words are in `words` and the frames in `lines`. Another language (Gujarati first) swaps this block with those two. Order ladder: `order` frames start each dish, `list.next` joins things in any order, `then` (the line key) joins the next step of a sequence ("Ne poi {x}.", a draft from Zafar, Mum to confirm), `no` says leave-it-out rows ("{x} na.", Mum 26 Sept, B1: two words, like `and`, so a hidden no-row isn't given away by its shape), and `then_word` is the linker's word id: from its word stage 3 the ladder stops drawing the sequence and only the spoken linker tells you the order.

gender._about: Words agree with a noun's gender (words[id].gender: he | she | unknown). A word with `forms` ({he, she}) takes the form for the noun it goes with: "one" (hakro/hakri) and describing words (wadho/wadhi). Unknown gender (most nouns until the family says) takes the word's own `kutchi`; the order frame Muke {x} khape is the informal one and never changes (docs/kutchi-grammar-notes.md 1).

verdicts._about: Words shown over the action after a timing or a pour (English UI). Mechanics name them by key.

pantry._about: Wave 6 (docs/UX-PRINCIPLES.md 7): Nani's list from the pantry, the smallest round and the first thing a new player does. She says the first thing with Muke {x} de (give me), then Ne {x} for the rest, in any order; you tap each into the basket. Level 1 = three things from the kitchen basics, each level one more (and a fuller shelf: mechanics.fetch.levels). free: false keeps it out of customers' orders.
pantry.name: ph-pantry
pantry.how: Listen to what Nani needs, then tap each one into the basket.

chai.name: cook-chai
chai._about: The Chai tray (js/cook/stations/chai-tray.js): a cup for each person on the tray, each with their face. The customer orders chai at the counter; at the tray each person says how they like theirs (dudh or dudh na; Muke chai me {n} khun khape or khun na; plain, elchi waari chai or aadu waari chai; at level 4 also half or full), so those rows wait for the tray (`when`). Wave 6 levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one cup; 2 = two; 3 = three; 4 = three plus half/full. Each cup is one card with a fixed shape (`card`). Tastes are only a bias (tasteChance).
chai.how: Each person says how they like their chai. Make every cup their way.

card._about: Wave 6: a cup's card always has these slots, in this order (an empty slot when the chai is plain). `optional` slots show only when someone in this order has them.

maani._about: The Maani line (data/stations/maani-line.json): which kind and how many, in Kutchi. The tally's kinds are said in a random order; the bowls always offer both doughs. Wave 6 levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one maani (which kind: listen); 2 = two, any mix; 3 = three with both kinds, and a second tawa; 4 = big/small (wadhi/nindhi, she-forms: maani is a she-word), a compound kind ph-big+cook-maani said 'ba wadhi maani'. One card per maani (`cards`).
maani.name: cook-maani
maani.how: Listen for which maani and how many. Roll each one, then cook it on the tawa.

daal.name: cook-daal
daal._about: Chop: the order names which vegetables go in (dungri, tameto, marcha: several from level 1); Nani says how many of each at the board. Level 1 chops them all in one timed round; levels 2-3 split the round with a switch (the chop mechanic's `phases`).
daal.how: Chop what they say, add the spices in the order Nani says, then stir.

chaat.name: ph-chaat
chaat.how: Build the bowl in the order they say. Leave out what they say no to.

samosa.name: ph-samosa
samosa.how: Fill them with what they say, fold them, then fry them.

mishkaki.name: ph-mishkaki
mishkaki._about: The order says how many skewers of each kind (a tally: "ba lakri gos, hakri lakri boga": lakri, the skewer, is the tally's `unit`, a she-word, so one is hakri), and when there's a mixed one its pieces in order (Pela gos, ne poi …): meat and the three vegetables, never the same piece twice running. Wave 6 (docs/UX-PRINCIPLES.md): one card per skewer, always four dots (`cards`), a mixed one naming its pieces on its dots (`cardOf`); the grill is two jobs, one at a time (thread every skewer, then "Go to the barbecue" and grill them; the juggle of both at once is the optional level 4); no chips on the grill (they stay in samosa + fry). Levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one skewer (meat or veg: listen); 2 = two; 3 = two or three, one may be mixed; 4 = three or four, up to two mixed, threading and grilling at once.
mishkaki.how: Thread each skewer the way they say. Then take them to the barbecue.

mechanics._about: Difficulty as data. Each mechanic's levels: level 1 is the Phase A game exactly; each later level lists only what changes. `profiles` hold settings for one use of a mechanic (pour into a cup). Upgrades change knobs through upgrades[].knobs. Timings are fractions of a ring (0-1) and rates are ring-fills per second. A combined station's own levels can live in data/stations/<id>.json.

levels._pourMs: Wave 6b: a tap pours one measure (to the next dashed line) in this long; the hold knobs (rate, auto, stickMs, minPour, bandScale, spillScore) are only for Cook.Pour.hold, which Cook no longer uses

thread._about: The Mishkaki grill's board (js/cook/mechanics/thread.js): pieces per skewer (the mixed pattern is 4 long too), decoy bowls from decoyPool (a piece that fits no skewer), and how long after Nani's spoken hint the piece glows (being shown costs the ear star).

grill._about: The Mishkaki grill (js/cook/mechanics/grill.js): each skewer's ring (band, rate in rings per second, rateSpread so they drift apart), turns before the lift, how many cook at once (spots), rack slots (fixed per level, never the number ordered), burntScore, and ignoreBelow (a tap this early in a ring is ignored: no accidental double taps).

art._about: Painted props to load besides the built-in ones and those named by a word's image (assets/cook/props/<name>.webp), e.g. a new dish's omelette-raw / omelette-done.

sprites._about: Painted item sprites (ChatGPT batch 1, build/reports/chatgpt-batch-1.md), wired over the drawn Phase A art, which stays as the fallback (js/cook/art.js). items: item id (a word id, or a thing: pan, tawa, glass…) -> state -> file stem in `dir` (<stem>.png is the source, <stem>.webp what the game loads; build/sprites_webp.py makes the webp: trimmed, max `max` px, or exactly `w` px wide for a prop it replaces, `square` makes it a circle's box). A word's `bowl` is how it shows on a worktop row (the pantry keeps its props and drawn bowls: its shelves need front views), `whole` flies in the chop, `raw`/`grilled`/`charred` go on a skewer. art: a drawn Art key -> item.state (frames: bake the sprite into the drawing's canvas, at box [x, y, w, h], so every scale and crop in the code still fits). props: a painted prop (assets/cook/props) -> item.state loaded under the prop's name instead. vessels: where a vessel sprite's opening is, as fractions of the sprite [cx, cy, rx, ry] plus the depth of its inside (the liquid and the dashed lines sit in it); size scales it against the drawn one's opening; filled: the sprite already shows what's in it (the kadai's oil), so no liquid is drawn over it. bg: a worktop view -> a 1600x900 webp in assets/cook/bg (day only: the game has no evening or night yet). need: what a station or mechanic loads before it builds (only those; anything else falls back to the drawing and loads for next time). Left out on purpose (failed QA or pending a redo): veg-dungri-whole-t, veg-dungri-peeled-t, tool-velan-t, tool-chakla-t, vessel-thali-t. tools: a painted tool drawn into a drawn hand (Wave 6b).

tools._about: Wave 6b: a painted tool in a drawn hand (js/cook/art.js): a drawn Art key -> item.state. The sprite (drawn corner to corner, tip top-left) is turned upright into the hand's own canvas, so every scale and angle in the code stays the same; the skewer's bamboo stick replaces the drawn one above its wooden handle (js/cook/mechanics/grill.js). Not yet: the velan and chakla (batch 1 failed QA: a Western pin with handles, a 3/4-view board; batch 2 redraws them).

lookalike_groups._about: Pass me shows three pictures from ONE group, so the answer never stands out as the odd one out (docs/cook-with-nani-kutchi-audit.md). Groups keep photos with photos and drawn bowls with bowls, so the picture style gives nothing away either.

star_sets._about: Each game mode supplies its own star icons (icon names from js/cook/ui.js ICON). Cook: the 'cooked well' star is a chef's hat. Find it (planned): a magnifying glass.

hand.name: Cooked well
hand.tip: Cooked well: nothing spilt or burnt

relaxed.name: No help
relaxed.tip: No help: no hints, reveals or translations

busy.name: Quick
busy.tip: Quick: served before their patience ran out

ear.name: Understood
ear.tip: Understood: found what they asked for

hand.name: Sharp eyes
hand.tip: Sharp eyes: found it without a wrong pick

calm._about: Wave 5 (clarity and calm): how much Nani says. quietMs: at the start of every station she says nothing for this long (no hints) so the player can work it out. hintMs: how long you can hesitate before she says the word again, by word stage 1-4 (then it glows a few seconds later). passMeChance: the chance she asks for something at a safe moment (never in the first order of a session; at most once an order at level 1). Wave 6: bulbMs = how long the light bulb shows English, by the order's level (5, 3, 2, 1 s); coachSteps = how many moves the first-time overlay shows at a station before it's gone; uiAfter = after how many orders the stars and the light bulb fade in (a new player's first order has only the order card).

lab._about: Wave 6b (the quality pass, Q4 and Q9 item 6): the Station lab lists the nine kept stations (lab entry keys, in this order); every other entry (the sub-mechanics: pour, boil, count, roll, flip, thread, grill…) sits under 'Parts' for testing. Knead is cut (its file isn't loaded).

onboard._about: Wave 6b (docs/UX-PRINCIPLES.md 8 and 10): the first-time onboarding script for each kept station, run by the shared kit (js/shared/onboard.js) through js/cook/coach.js. Each step is one move the overlay shows: everything dims except the next thing to do (the station's own 'what to do next', Cook.expect), a ghost hand does `do` once (tap, swipe, stir, roll, hold), the child does it, then the next. After the last step the overlay is gone at that station for good (once per profile). `what` says what the step is, for people reading this. Only the guided first time (a dish's first order; the Station lab with 'Nani helps'). Keys are the stations' own keys (Cook.Stations.begin).

fetch.what: the first thing on Nani's list, on the shelf

chai-tray.what: the water jug: one tap pours water into the pan, up to the line
the big knob: the burner lights
the first thing this cup's person asked for (the milk jug, the sugar bowl or an extra)

maani-line.what: the dough bowl they asked for
roll the ball up and down until it fills the circle

thread.what: a bowl: the piece slides down the skewer
the last piece: the skewer is full

grill.what: a skewer on the rack: onto the grill
turn it again on the green
lift it onto the plate on the green

tadka.what: the first spice she said, into the hot oil
the next one (or the pan: tip it into the pot)

stir.what: drag the ladle round the pot, counting the laps

assemble.what: the first topping they said: the bottom layer

fill.what: a spoon of the first filling they said

fry.what: lift it out on the green

tips._about: One short 'Next time' tip per missed star on the result card. Plain words, no numbers.

ear.no: Leave out what they said no to
ear.order: Do them in the order they said
ear.count: Make as many as they asked for
ear.speed: Stir at the speed Nani says
ear.shown: Have a go before Nani shows you
ear.passme: Listen for what Nani asks for
ear.wrong: Listen for each word, then pick it

hand.pour: Stop pouring at the dashed line
hand.boil: Turn the knob down when the ring is green
hand.tawa: Flip when the ring reaches green
hand.fry: Lift each one out when its ring is green
hand.grill: Turn the skewer when its ring is green
hand.roll: Roll until it just fills the circle
hand.stir speed: Stir at the speed Nani says
hand.knead: Keep pressing until the dough is smooth
hand.default: Take your time with your hands
hand.tadka: Add the next spice before the oil smokes
hand.chop missed: Slice each one Nani names before it falls

third.busy: Serve before the ring runs out
third.relaxed: Have a go without help first
